name: Kilbourne Hole, New Mexico, USA
status: known planetary analog; first terrain prototype

source.acquisition_period: Primarily 2011–2015; exact local acquisition and infill not established
source.nominal_spacing: 1 arc-second, approximately 30 metres; longitude spacing varies with latitude

grid.order: row-major; north to south, west to east

local_frame.note: Directions follow UTM grid north/east; not an exact geodetic ENU frame.

physics.note: Material parameters require independent measurements or explicitly labelled simulation settings; gravity is a scenario setting, not supplied by the DEM.

analog.basis: NASA field-training and volcanic-process analog literature; no matched Mars or lunar DEM comparison has been performed

limitations: 30 m data resolves broad landforms, not rocks, wheel-scale hazards, caves or overhangs.
DSM may include vegetation and structures; quality/error masks were not acquired.
Slopes are finite-difference estimates on the resampled grid; cliffs are smoothed.
No measured soil mechanics, imagery texture, climate layers or planetary terrain are included.
Display material is a neutral illustration, not a land-cover classification.
